Published online:
September 11, 2026

Geographic focus:
United States

Temporal focus:
T1. Historical report [YES] — August 2026 CPI/PPI data reported
T2. Forward-looking reporting short-term risks (next few weeks/months) [YES] — Fed September 15-16 meeting rate decision imminent
T3. Forward-looking reporting long-term risks (next quarters/years) [YES] — Tariff-driven inflation persistence, political pressure on Fed independence, November midterm implications

Synopsis:
August 2026 CPI came in at +0.4% MoM and +3.4% YoY, in line with forecasts, driven by a gasoline rebound. Core CPI eased slightly to +2.4% YoY. PPI data released a day prior showed strong upstream price pressures feeding into PCE. Oil back above $100/bbl and record diesel prices suggest inflation staying elevated. Markets are pricing ~70% odds of a 25bps hike at the upcoming Sep 15-16 FOMC meeting. Fed Chair Kevin Warsh has signaled more work to do on inflation, while President Trump is publicly pressuring the Fed to cut rates — a dynamic some analysts see as pushing the Fed to hike in order to assert independence.

Q05. Focus on the very latest information: What is the sentiment/tone including the very latest information on US interest rates?
Sentiment: 75 (More hawkish — CPI in-line but not cooling, PPI hot, oil above $100, Fed Chair Warsh signaling more tightening needed, and Fed independence pressure reinforcing a likely hike. No material dovish surprise in the data.)
